findings.issue_text: [High/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:230-255 (getForLogin) — Inconsistent return values between cache-hit and cache-miss paths: cache-miss results are wrapped via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but cache-hit models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) are not wrapped, so callers observe different model behavior (e.g., isEnabled(), organization-aware resolution) depending on cache state

[Medium/test_bug] OrganizationCacheTest.java:~383 and ~414 — getCleanup().addCleanup uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so cleanup targets a nonexistent provider (404) and the 21 created IDPs leak for the remainder of the suite run

[Medium/test_gap] OrganizationCacheTest.java — No test covers removal of a login-eligible IDP via remove(); only removal of a non-login IDP (idp-alias-1) is tested, leaving the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) path (including null-safe behavior and fresh idpDelegate.getByAlias lookup) untested

[Medium/test_gap] OrganizationCacheTest.java / LoginFilter — No test for an organization-linked IDP with BROKER_PUBLIC unset/false; the new predicate clause silently excludes such IDPs from getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, ...), and since all test IDPs set BROKER_PUBLIC=true, this behavior change is unverified

[Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — Potential NPE in the new predicate: idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) is evaluated whenever getOrganizationId() != null, and will throw if the model's config map is null (possible for models built from raw representations or deserialized cache entries)

[Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~99 (remove) — idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is now executed unconditionally on every remove even when the cache-hit branch could supply the model from CachedIdentityProvider, adding a storage lookup per removal

[Low/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~247-250 — In the fallback when a cached internal id no longer resolves (idp == null), the stale IdentityProviderListQuery entry is only invalidated transactionally, so concurrent reads in other transactions can keep re-observing the stale entry until commit, repeatedly triggering DB fallbacks; consider cache.invalidateObject (immediate) for consistency with the cached == null branch

[Low/concurrency] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~239-243 — The cached == null branch performs cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) (broadcasting cluster-wide invalidation that drops other organizations' cached searchKeys on other nodes) followed by a non-atomic re-add; the unconditional full-entry invalidation is unnecessary since chaining the new query with revision checks suffices

[Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~232-247 — The login list cache key omits organizationId and accumulates one entry per distinct organization searched inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery, unboundedly growing the cached query object per realm for realms with many organizations

[Low/doc_defect] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~392-404 — The javadoc for registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate does not fully match the implementation: the code also skips invalidation when the org id changes while the IDP remains login-eligible in ways the predicate can't distinguish (e.g., only BROKER_PUBLIC toggles for an org-linked IDP), which the Objects.equals(getOrganizationId()) check description doesn't cover

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:230-255 (getForLogin) — Inconsistent return values between cache-hit and cache-miss paths: cache-miss results are wrapped via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but cache-hit models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) are not wrapped, so callers observe different model behavior (e.g., isEnabled(), organization-aware resolution) depending on cache state

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path iterates cached IDs and returns the models from `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` directly, without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This is a concrete behavioral inconsistency within the method and can change observable `IdentityProviderModel` behavior depending on cache state (the diff even notes callers may see wrapped models, e.g. the added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check comment).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] OrganizationCacheTest.java — No test covers removal of a login-eligible IDP via remove(); only removal of a non-login IDP (idp-alias-1) is tested, leaving the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) path (including null-safe behavior and fresh idpDelegate.getByAlias lookup) untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove(String)` by fetching `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and then calling `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (which conditionally invalidates login caches via `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`). In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the only removal exercised is `idp-alias-1`, which was created with `enabled=false` (odd index) and thus is not login-eligible; the newly added invalidation path for removing a login-eligible IDP is therefore not covered. Additionally, the null-safe behavior when `getByAlias` returns null (predicate starts with `Objects::nonNull`) is also not exercised by the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] OrganizationCacheTest.java / LoginFilter — No test for an organization-linked IDP with BROKER_PUBLIC unset/false; the new predicate clause silently excludes such IDPs from getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, ...), and since all test IDPs set BROKER_PUBLIC=true, this behavior change is unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new clause to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` requiring org-linked IDPs to have `BROKER_PUBLIC` true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`). The new `testCacheIDPForLogin` only links IDPs to an org after setting `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` for all of them (loop `i >= 10`), so it never exercises the case of an org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` unset/false. That is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for newly added logic, not a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — Potential NPE in the new predicate: idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) is evaluated whenever getOrganizationId() != null, and will throw if the model's config map is null (possible for models built from raw representations or deserialized cache entries)

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new conjunct in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:

```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```

This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check when `getOrganizationId() != null`. If `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` can ever return `null`, this will throw an NPE and is a behavior change introduced by the diff. The diff itself doesn’t establish a non-null contract for `getConfig()`, so the risk is real even if not proven by the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~99 (remove) — idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is now executed unconditionally on every remove even when the cache-hit branch could supply the model from CachedIdentityProvider, adding a storage lookup per removal

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check, so it executes on every removal. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; on cache-hit it could use `CachedIdentityProvider` to invalidate by internalId. The new unconditional lookup adds an extra delegate/storage read per remove (even when `cached != null` could provide the model via `cached.getIdp()`), which is a concrete performance concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~247-250 — In the fallback when a cached internal id no longer resolves (idp == null), the stale IdentityProviderListQuery entry is only invalidated transactionally, so concurrent reads in other transactions can keep re-observing the stale entry until commit, repeatedly triggering DB fallbacks; consider cache.invalidateObject (immediate) for consistency with the cached == null branch

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin(...) implementation, when a cached internalId cannot be resolved (idp == null), the code calls realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey) and immediately falls back to idpDelegate.getForLogin(...). In the earlier “searchKey not yet cached” branch, it instead calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) before reloading. The finding correctly points out this inconsistency: the idp==null path does not perform immediate cache invalidation like the other branch, which could plausibly allow other concurrent transactions to keep seeing the stale IdentityProviderListQuery until the invalidation is applied. This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern, but it’s primarily a cache-consistency/performance behavior rather than a clearly provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~239-243 — The cached == null branch performs cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) (broadcasting cluster-wide invalidation that drops other organizations' cached searchKeys on other nodes) followed by a non-atomic re-add; the unconditional full-entry invalidation is unnecessary since chaining the new query with revision checks suffices

adjudication.rationale: The new getForLogin() cache path does call cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) in the branch where an IdentityProviderListQuery exists but query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null (i.e., a new organizationId/searchKey not yet cached). Since cacheKey is per realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)), invalidating that single entry necessarily drops any other already-cached searchKey results stored inside the same query object. The code then re-fetches and re-adds a new IdentityProviderListQuery, which is a non-atomic invalidate-then-add sequence and can cause avoidable cluster-wide churn/races (extra cache misses) even if not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~232-247 — The login list cache key omits organizationId and accumulates one entry per distinct organization searched inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery, unboundedly growing the cached query object per realm for realms with many organizations

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the cache key is `cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)` and does not include `organizationId` (or `searchKey`). The code then stores results per `searchKey` inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` (`query.getIDPs(searchKey)`), and if a new `searchKey` is requested it rebuilds the query with `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`, implying prior per-searchKey data can be retained/accumulated within the same cached object. This can cause the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` to grow with each distinct organization searched for a realm+mode until an invalidation occurs, which is a concrete performance/memory-scope concern introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~392-404 — The javadoc for registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate does not fully match the implementation: the code also skips invalidation when the org id changes while the IDP remains login-eligible in ways the predicate can't distinguish (e.g., only BROKER_PUBLIC toggles for an org-linked IDP), which the Objects.equals(getOrganizationId()) check description doesn't cover

adjudication.rationale: In `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, invalidation is skipped only when (a) both `original` and `updated` fail `getLoginPredicate()` or (b) both pass `getLoginPredicate()` **and** `Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())` is true. If the org id changes, condition (b) fails and the method invalidates all login caches. Also, toggling `BROKER_PUBLIC` for an org-linked IDP is part of the updated `getLoginPredicate()` (server-spi diff), so a change there will cause predicate mismatch and trigger invalidation, not skipping it. The finding’s claimed mismatch is not supported by the diff.
